Hello all! It's officially time to join this party - and I brought beer. Are there any great subverses that you love and can recommend?

So, in my eyes, the "root" of the problem with what's happening with reddit right now is that 1,000,000 might use a sub but only a handful of mods have "government" powers over the sub. Despite the majority of the sub wanting or not wanting some content left alone, the power of the decision is ultimately in the hands of a few people. It's the same system with voat right now.

We know the site admins are good people, and, in general, with the crowd that's been attracted, I don't expect any mods going on banning sprees anytime soon. But what will stop this from happening 2 years in the future? What's to stop a couple of people from oppressing an entire sub?

Here's where the idea comes in. It's the internet so it's very easy to vote (voat?) just by simply clicking a button. So I think it would be good to offload some of the power of the mods and put in the hands of the majority.

How exactly will that work? That's the tricky part. As a random proposition, every subverse could have a page something like /v/news/meta/ where you can submit a poll/vote and then users can vote on polls and also upvoat them. And if a poll reaches XXX upvoats, then some action should be taken on it. But, again, this is a very sketchy idea based on a pretty fuzzy concept.

And what exactly is there to vote on?

The most obvious one is the subverse rules. Every subverse has some kind of rules like "no links from site XX", "no discussion of topic XX because it belongs elsewhere", etc. These rules exist for good reason, but where does one draw the line between "reasonable" and "arbitrary"? Wouldn't it be nice if these were community driven? You can start a vote to add/repeal rule and if it gets upvoted enough on /subverse/meta/ then the mods should honor it and enforce it.

Another one is to "revive" a deleted thread. You'd go to a place akin to /r/undelete and flag a post to be brought back to the sub. If it gets enough attention (like a very high number of tags/upvotes) then it would be reinstalled on the subverse and be put into "protected" status

Lastly, a mod purge. This one would be very hard to pull off. Requires a very high % of subverse users to vote on it (in such a way that it'd never happen unless it was a subverse crisis). Then, if it reaches the limit, site admins would step in and mediate the process for putting in new mods in power. This would be the kind of thing that never actually happens unless shit completely hits the fan in a sub

And, if it wasn't clear, I'm saying that the voting is something optional for more "involved" users of a sub. The average person would not need to interact with it if they don't want to and, in general, the mods would continue with their day-to-day mod tasks.

In general, I rambled a lot and these were just some general ideas that weren't very well defined. But I'm just trying to open a point of discussion. Wouldn't it be nice for there to be more "democracy" in Voat, especially since Voat advertises itself as a "platform for free speech". What better way to promote free speech than with some form of democracy?
Wouldn't it be nice if we implemented some form of democracy for subverses?
